one_liner: JIT-generated small GEMM, batch-reduce GEMM and element-wise kernels; DL layers built on it beat MKL-DNN by 1.1-1.7x.
what_it_does: A C library (with C++ overloads and Fortran bindings) that JIT-generates kernels for small dense/sparse matrix multiplication, batch-reduce GEMM (BRGEMM) and element-wise unary/binary/ternary ops, collectively called Tensor Processing Primitives (TPP). You dispatch a kernel for a fixed shape and datatype (libxsmm_dispatch_gemm / _brgemm / _meltw_*), get a function pointer, and call it repeatedly; a BLAS-compatible libxsmm_?gemm wrapper also exists. It is not a DNN library itself: since 2.0 the convolution/FC/LSTM operators live in the companion repo libxsmm-dnn.
how_it_is_fast: Runtime code specialization: for each (M,N,K,ld,datatype,flags) it emits machine code fully unrolled for that shape, using the best ISA found via CPUID (AVX-512/VNNI/BF16, AMX, NEON/SVE/SME, RVV, POWER10 MMA), with operand prefetch hints for batches. The batch-reduce GEMM kernel (C = beta*C + sum_i A_i*B_i) keeps the output block in registers across a whole sequence of A/B block pairs, so higher-level layers become loops around one tuned microkernel instead of separate GEMM calls with C round-trips through memory.
when_to_use: Many repeated multiplications of small matrices, roughly (M*N*K)^(1/3) <= 64, e.g. block-sparse or spectral-element/DG codes (CP2K/DBCSR, SeisSol, Nek5000, PETSc block kernels).
Writing custom CPU DL operators (conv, FC, RNN, attention blocks) as blocked loops around BRGEMM plus fused element-wise TPPs.
Low-precision CPU kernels (BF16, FP16, FP8 variants, int8/int4, MX formats) on AVX-512 VNNI/AMX, Arm SVE/SME or POWER10 without hand-writing assembly.
Shipping one binary that should pick the right ISA at runtime ('build once, deploy everywhere') without -march flags.
when_not_to_use: Large GEMMs: there is no multi-level M/N/K cache blocking; large sizes generate excessive unrolled code and miss cache tiling, so use MKL/OpenBLAS/BLIS.
You want ready-made DL layers: in 2.0 they moved to libxsmm-dnn and the PyTorch integration to tpp-pytorch-extension; the core repo only gives primitives.
Full BLAS semantics: JIT GEMM kernels are limited to alpha=1, beta in {0,1}, transA='N' (BLAS-style wrapper falls back otherwise).
Windows deployments needing more than the MM domain: the Compatibility wiki lists Windows JIT as MM-only without prefetch kernels.

integration.form: static lib | shared lib (GNU Make or CMake 3.13+), or header-only via libxsmm_source.h
integration.dependencies: none for the core; libxsmmext and the Fortran module need an OpenMP runtime; Fortran compiler optional (FORTRAN=0)
integration.min_toolchain: C compiler; GCC 5.1+ recommended (older GCC degrades CPUID-dispatched code); Clang, Intel; Fortran 2003 for the module
integration.platforms: x86-64 (SSE through AVX-512/AMX), AArch64 (NEON/SVE/SME), RISC-V RVV, POWER10 ppc64le; Linux, macOS, FreeBSD, Windows (limited JIT)
integration.thread_safety: Thread-safe: core routines can be called concurrently; threading-runtime agnostic (PGI and TinyCC builds have caveats).
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — libxsmm_?gemm is BLAS-ABI compatible for small GEMM, but it does not replace oneDNN; DL layers must be composed from TPPs or taken from libxsmm-dnn

gotchas: Shapes over the JIT limits (operand >2 GiB, or >2 MB stack scratch for VNNI reformatting) silently fall back to a slow reference kernel; check libxsmm_get_kernel_info or run with LIBXSMM_VERBOSE=2.
The public header is generated at build time (not in the repo); header-only use exposes internals and compiles your settings (e.g. NDEBUG) into LIBXSMM.
No error returns from the frontend: failures are reported only via verbose mode, so a NULL kernel pointer must be checked by the caller.
With verbosity on it installs SIGABRT/SIGSEGV handlers; set LIBXSMM_SIGNAL=0 if the host application owns signals.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick LIBXSMM over Fastor when shapes are runtime values or you need low-precision/AMX/SVE kernels rather than compile-time fixed-size C++ tensors (Fastor can even use LIBXSMM as its JIT backend); pick it over the AVX512 DGEMM tutorial kernels or llamafile tinyBLAS when you need a maintained, multi-ISA library of small/batched GEMMs rather than large-GEMM or LLM-specific kernels.
verified_claims_summary: In Georganas et al. (IPDPS 2020, arXiv 1906.06440), Intel authors built LSTM, fully-connected and ResNet-50 convolution layers on LIBXSMM's batch-reduce GEMM and measured them against 2019 MKL-DNN on a 28-core Xeon Platinum 8180 with Intel compiler 18.0.0: LSTM 1.2-1.3x faster forward and 1.1-1.7x backward/update, FC 1.09-1.36x, ResNet-50 conv efficiency 83% vs 81%. Flags were not stated and the paper notes the gains shrink for large matrices.
status_note: Actively developed (commits in late Sept 2026, 2.0 release restructured the repo) and BSD-3-Clause, packaged in Debian/Fedora/Ubuntu/Spack/Conda; note the benchmarked DL operators now live in libxsmm-dnn.
